blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Re-reviewed 2026-08-08 at Ethereum block 25712294: HOME proxy 0xb8919522331c59f5c16bdfaa6a121a6e03a91f62 pointed to verified Pool16 implementation 0x366049d336e73cfaf39c6a933780ca4c96ea084c behind ProxyAdmin 0x5729890f78c07bc2d1c09345001f6c1f0c9d7d6f. ProxyAdmin owner 0xa42f6fb68607048dde54fcd53d2195cc8ca5f486 remained a five-owner, threshold-three legacy multisig. The current implementation and exact ABI expose standard transfer/transferFrom behavior but no blacklist, pause, freeze, seize, allowlist, or privileged holder-burn path. The official repository contains mortgage-originator agreements, but no current token-holder terms that positively exclude an issuer-level legal restriction were available; absence of such terms cannot support a false verdict. The direct review therefore remains honestly possible, while the live no-timelock 3/5 upgrade path is verified as restrictable in the transfer overlay.
blacklistabilityReview.upstreamSuppressionRationale: Mortgage, USDC liquidity, and foreclosure risks can impair HOME's backing or redemption value, but the reviewed current token implementation gives neither the mortgage obligors nor reserve-asset issuers a direct holder restriction path on HOME. Those exposures remain backing and dependency risks; future token restrictions through the live proxy upgrade authority are represented in the transfer overlay.
